summary: Failsafe fallback + state snapshot plan for mixed quantization and batching cache conflict
description: Summary: NimbusDocs reported a sudden increase in 95th percentile token latency and intermittent streaming disconnects after we rolled a new mixed quantization profile with aggressive kv-prefetch. They are on Dedicated capacity. This ticket captures a conservative, testable fallback that preserves cache state where possible and gives an emergency path back to stable behavior without full workload interruption.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs high-concurrency inference workload (80 concurrent connections) hitting /v1/chat/stream with model llama-2-7b-q4_keras-compat.
2) Deploy quant profile 'q4-mixed-prefetch-v2' + batching config: target_batch_tokens=1024, max_latency_ms=60.
3) Observe steady-state then see 95th latency climb from ~70ms to >400ms and occasional 502s from worker restarts.
4) Reverting quant profile to previous 'q4-mixed-prefetch-v1' temporarily reduces errors but latency remains elevated until caches are flushed.
5) Reproduces intermittently on us-west region under identical traffic shapes.

observed_impact: Customer-facing production latency regression (95p token latency >400ms), intermittent streaming disconnects, elevated GPU utilization on a subset of workers, and increased error budget burn for SLA targets.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: aggressive kv-prefetch combined with the new mixed quantization variant changed memory/compute characteristics causing poorer kernel selection and cache-miss amplification.
Checked node-level metrics: affected workers show consistent mem spike during prefix fetch and a surge in host->device transfer rates concurrently with latency spikes.
Reproduced locally with a traffic replay against a staging pool using q4-mixed-prefetch-v2; when kv-prefetch enabled, p95 rose ~5x vs pre-change.
Kernel selection logs show fallback to slower attention kernel for sequences >512 when running q4-mixed-prefetch-v2 under burst traffic.
No evidence of application-layer bug in router; 502s correlate with worker process restarts (OOM killer) on two nodes.
Related PR noted earlier tweaks to prefetch batch window and introduced a new allocator path (see PR above).
Potential risk: a blind full-cache flush will drop warm KVs and spike downstream latency; must avoid global full flush for dedicated customers if possible.
Decision: prepare incremental, deterministic fallback with state snapshot and staged toggles rather than immediate full revert.
proposed_action_plan: Step A - Snapshot: capture per-worker KV-index snapshot and active batch histogram for the past 10 minutes. Command: /usr/local/bin/collect_kv_snapshot --worker=ALL --out=/tmp/nimbus_snapshot_2026-03-13.tgz
Step B - Staged toggle: disable kv-prefetch on a subset (10%) of nodes in the pool and observe p95/CPU/mem over 5m windows.
Step C - If improvement: roll kv-prefetch disable to additional 30% then 60% with 5m soak between waves.
Step D - Quant profile fallback: for nodes showing no improvement after prefetched disable, roll model variant to 'q4-stable-v1' with same model checksum to avoid cold-start recompiles.
Step E - Batching adjustment: reduce target_batch_tokens to 512 and raise max_latency_ms to 120ms on impacted routes as temporary mitigation to reduce batch accumulation pressure.
Step F - Post-fix: once stable, re-enable prefetch on a small ring (5%) with conservative prefetch window and monitor for regression for 24h before wider rollout.
Step G - Follow-up: schedule a patch to allocator logic and kernel selection heuristics; link to FR for runtime team.
short_term_workaround: Apply staged kv-prefetch disable (Step B) to reduce memory pressure without global cache wipe.
Pin affected routes to q4-stable-v1 as necessary to prevent worker OOMs.
Temporarily relax batching aggressiveness to avoid large in-flight batches that drive mem spikes.
Increase autoscaler headroom for the dedicated pool to provide capacity buffer during remediation.
Notify customer of progressive mitigation plan and expected impact windows.
Open monitoring alert to page on p95 token latency >250ms for more than 3m post-change.
long_term_recommendations: Introduce a per-tenant kv-prefetch safety budget that prevents prefetch concurrency from exceeding worker memory headroom.
Add pre-deploy canary against representative traffic shape that exercises batch/caching interactions for quantized variants.
Expand kernel-selection telemetry to include quant variant and prefetch window for easier offline triage.
Create a documented 'snapshot-and-fallback' runbook for Dedicated customers with state-preserving toggles.
Implement an automated staged rollback tool that toggles flags and monitors SLA signals with built-in abort conditions.
